newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB 1996 ord pre-tax profits up about 30%.
newsitem.headline: UCB 1996 ord pre-tax profits up about 30%.

text.p: Belgian chemicals, drugs and films group UCB said on Wednesday 1996 group ordinary profit before taxes grew by about 30 percent to almost 5.5 billion Belgian francs.
The figure compares with a current profit of 4.2 billion booked over 1995.

Announcing provisional 1996 results, chief executive officer Georges Jacobs told reporters consolidated net profit, including one large exceptional gain, would be "slightly less" than six billion francs. In 1995 UCB had net profit of 3.4 billion.
The 1996 net profit figure included an intra-group share transaction earlier this year, which netted UCB 1.7 billion Belgian francs that was booked as an extraordinary gain in the first half.

The deal involved the sale of a 4.68 percent stake in UCB by Banque du Luxembourg to UCB Financiere, which under company rules could not hold on to the shares and was forced to sell the stake via UCB on to holding company Financiere d'Obourg.
The deal raised Financiere d'Obourg's stake in UCB to over 30 percent. Under an agreement with Banque du Luxembourg it was done at the price at which the bank bought the shares in 1988.
Since then UCB stock has risen substantially, resulting in a capital gain which was free of tax because it involved a Luxembourg company and companies within the same group.

The capital gain from UCB's sale of its packaging division to Amcor Group of Australia would be spread over two years. For UCB this meant it would book 200 million francs in gains in 1996 and 200 million in 1997.
Jacobs said 400 million francs had been set aside in provisions "to adapt structures" to the sale of the packaging division and of fine chemicals operations.

Jacobs said pharma sector sales were more than 21 billion francs in 1996, up from 18.7 billion in 1995, due particularly to royalties from the sale of star anti-allergy drug Zyrtec in the U.S. Ordinary profit in the sector was almost 3.4 billion francs, up from 2.7 billion in 1995.

Chemicals sales were above 19 billion francs in 1996, up from 17 billion in 1995. Volumes were better in the second half than in the first, which suffered from a slowdown in Europe. Ordinary profit exceeded 1.4 billion after 1.17 billion in 1995.
Film sector sales reached 10 billion francs, down from 15.9 billion in 1995.
Jacobs noted the 1996 figure should be adjusted for the sale of the packaging division, which had turnover of 10 billion.
Ordinary profits in packaging were close to 600 million francs, up from 417 million in 1995.
"I foresee steady growth in all three sectors, a positive trend in all three sectors," he said, adding that in the world economy there were "certain hopes of improvement."
Final 1996 figures are due after the April 11 management board meeting, which will also make a recommendation on the dividend payout to the annual shareholders meeting.
